content:
Often when I'm studying a project in detail, I like to start with a skeleton document that has the structure of the directory tree of the source code. Then, as I study the code I add my own comment or summaries of what the code is doing.

To aid in this, I've created a python script, versotreedoc.py, that walks a directory tree and creates a verso program that will create a document with the directory structure. You can execute it either in the top-level directory of the project to be documented, or in a desired subdirectory.

The script my be found at https://github.com/richardlford/versotreedoc.

Use the --help option to see how to use it (or look at the README.md which also shows the help).
The Examples/versodoc directory shows an example of the output of the tools. Note that it
is intended that the use would then start reading the code and filling in the "TODO"s.

To try out the example, you would use the following commands, assuming you are in a
scratch directory:

git clone https://github.com/richardlford/versotreedoc
cd versotreedoc/Examples/versodoc
lake exe internals
python serve.py

and then in a browser open "http://0.0.0.0:8000"
